cf.title: Make COPY format extendable: Extract COPY TO format implementations

input.subject: Make COPY format extendable: Extract COPY TO format implementations

verdict_reasoning: No objection survived at levels 1a or 1b: the problem is stated and demand is shown across several years. Four fixable level 2 objections survived. maintenance-fit-2 (options accepted with no effect) and maintenance-fit-3 (no in-tree format that moves bytes) are the strongest, followed by replication-ondisk-1, replication-ondisk-3 and maintenance-fit-4. These are design points a committer who knows COPY can settle; none requires a different proposal.

brief.title: Let extensions register custom COPY formats
brief.problem: COPY TO/FROM supports only text, csv and binary, and users have asked for JSON lines, Apache Arrow, Avro, Parquet and ORC. The author wants such formats to live in extensions, because they depend on external libraries and may not be written in C. The author also wants faster custom formats than conversions through text.
brief.proposed_design: Built-in formats already go through CopyToRoutine/CopyFromRoutine callbacks, committed earlier. The current v3 set (Sawada) moves the COPY state structs into a public header and adds a C registration API that an extension calls in _PG_init(). It also adds an opaque per-format state pointer, a per-option callback, a whole-options validation callback and a test module.
user_visible_surface: COPY option FORMAT accepts a format name registered by a loaded extension.
C API: RegisterCopyCustomFormat() with CopyToRoutine and CopyFromRoutine, called from _PG_init().
New header copy_state.h exposing CopyFromStateData and CopyToStateData, with an opaque format_private pointer.
Callbacks for format options: one per option, one to validate all options after processing.
Proposed exports of CopySendData(), CopySendEndOfRow() and CopyGetData() (reviewer diff, not yet in v3).
author_claims: The refactoring keeps behavior and tests unchanged.
The first benchmark showed no significant loss for text, csv and binary COPY TO at 100K to 10M rows.
Unqualified text, csv and binary always use the built-in formats, which keeps pg_dump output compatible.
Registration through _PG_init() avoids search_path problems and is secure by design.
Later benchmarks by Tomas Vondra and Sutou showed differences mostly within 5% with no reproducible trend.
brief.thread_state: Design moved from SQL handler functions to _PG_init() registration with support from Paquier and Sawada; Andres Freund raised performance concerns that no one answered conclusively. Two reviews of v3 (Manu, Joao Rito) found that extensions cannot move bytes without exporting the I/O functions, the test module fails on current master, and v3 needs a rebase.
unclear: The proposal does not say how a custom format should handle ON_ERROR, reject_limit, log_verbosity and cur_lineno.
Text/CSV-only options such as DELIMITER and HEADER are accepted silently with a custom format; the intended rule is not stated.
The thread has no agreed answer on whether a COPY FROM format may read copy_file directly for random access, as Parquet needs.
No committer has stated that the performance concern from Andres Freund is resolved.
Format IDs for progress reporting or statistics are deferred; the plan for them is open.
SGML documentation for the API and for the FORMAT option is missing.

prior_attempts.title: Adding Support for Copy callback functionality on COPY TO api
prior_attempts.quote: This feedback has not been answered after two weeks, so I have marked the patch as returned with feedback.
prior_attempts.reason: The author did not answer review feedback for two weeks, so the patch was returned with feedback. The open review points were to run pgindent, to add an in-tree user of the callback, and to have the callback return the number of bytes written and report failure.
prior_attempts.what_is_different: P3 added only a destination callback for COPY TO. This proposal registers whole formats in both directions. P3 ended because review comments went unanswered, which does not apply to this thread.

objections.title: Every new COPY option needs a decision in every custom format
objections.failure_scenario: A user runs COPY with FORMAT ndjson, ON_ERROR ignore, and DELIMITER '|'. Both options are accepted, have no effect, and a bad row still aborts with "line 0". When core later adds another option like reject_limit, each custom format accepts it silently until its author notices.
objections.argument: Message #341 shows DELIMITER, HEADER, NULL and FORCE_QUOTE accepted and ignored, and ON_ERROR accepted but not applied. The built-in checks are skipped for custom formats, so core has no way to reject options a format does not support. Each future COPY option then becomes a silent gap in every format until someone notices.
objections.author_must_show: What rule makes core reject a COPY option that a custom format does not declare support for, including ON_ERROR and future options?

critic.reasoning: Message #341 shows DELIMITER, HEADER, NULL and FORCE_QUOTE accepted with no effect, and ON_ERROR ignore accepted while a bad row still fails. v3 leaves rejection to each format's validation callback, and the proposal states no default rule in core.

objections.title: No in-tree format that moves bytes to guard the API
objections.failure_scenario: A committer changes how CopyGetData or CopySendEndOfRow handles the frontend or PROGRAM destination. The in-tree test module only raises NOTICEs, so it still passes. Out-of-tree formats break, and the project learns about it from bug reports after release.
objections.argument: Message #340 found that v3 exports no I/O functions, so the test module cannot write or read data, and the module fails on master. Message #341 confirms both points. A NOTICE-only module cannot show that real formats keep working, which is the concern recorded in [P8]. [P3] was also asked for an in-tree user of a new COPY callback.
objections.author_must_show: Will the series include an in-tree format that reads and writes real rows through the exported functions on file, frontend and PROGRAM paths?

precedents.title: ctidscan as an example of custom-scan
Adding Support for Copy callback functionality on COPY TO api

critic.reasoning: Messages #340 and #341 show the in-tree module only raises NOTICEs, which hid the missing I/O exports. [P3] supports the request for an in-tree user; [P8] concerned the usefulness of the custom-scan interface and must not be used as support.

objections.title: Custom format names stored in file_fdw options have no catalog anchor
objections.failure_scenario: A DBA creates a file_fdw foreign table with format 'ndjson' and loads the library only through LOAD. pg_dump emits the table, and on restore or during pg_upgrade's schema restore the file_fdw validator rejects it with 'COPY format "ndjson" not recognized'. A later removal of the library from shared_preload_libraries leaves the table failing at query time.
objections.argument: Message #341 shows that file_fdw accepts a custom format and that COPY fails when the library is not loaded. The format name is then persisted in ftoptions, but registration lives only in backend memory, so pg_depend and pg_dump know nothing about it. The proposal does not say how restore, pg_upgrade or library removal should behave for objects that name such a format.
objections.author_must_show: How does a file_fdw table using a custom format survive pg_dump, pg_restore and pg_upgrade when the library is not preloaded during the restore?

critic.reasoning: Message #341 confirms both halves: file_fdw stores a custom format name, and the name fails in a session without the library. Message #294 accepted the preload requirement for COPY commands, but the thread does not discuss restore of stored options.

objections.title: Wire protocol format code for custom formats is not defined
objections.failure_scenario: A client driver runs COPY TO STDOUT with an Arrow format and reads CopyOutResponse. If the server reports the overall format as text (0), a driver that treats text COPY data as character data in client_encoding can mangle the binary stream. The user finds out when the received file does not parse.
objections.argument: CopyOutResponse and CopyInResponse carry an overall format and per-column codes that only distinguish text and binary. Message #8 asked how column-oriented formats would work at the protocol level, and the visible material does not answer it. Message #341 tested \copy only with ndjson, which is text, so a binary format through the frontend path is untested.
objections.author_must_show: Which overall and per-column format codes does the server send in CopyOutResponse and CopyInResponse for a custom format, and who chooses them?

critic.reasoning: CopyOutResponse and CopyInResponse carry a text or binary code, and the visible v3 material does not say what a custom format sends. Message #10 answered message #8 only about row groups, and message #341 tested the frontend path only with a text format.

objections.title: Exported COPY I/O functions may block future COPY speedups
objections.failure_scenario: A developer wants to rework COPY FROM buffering, for example by parsing directly from raw_buf in batches. Extensions now call CopyGetData and read copy_file directly, as message #341 proposes for Parquet. The rework either breaks those extensions or has to keep the old per-call interface alive.
objections.argument: Message #309 asks about the COPY speedups this design forecloses, separately from the measured overhead. Message #310 answers only about indirection layers, and message #332 says that question is still open. Exporting CopyGetData, CopySendData and copy_file access fixes the current I/O layer as a contract.
objections.author_must_show: Which planned changes to COPY buffering or I/O would still be possible once CopyGetData, CopySendData and copy_file are part of the extension API?

critic.reasoning: Message #310 answered message #309 only about indirection, and message #332 says the question of which COPY improvements the design blocks is still open. No message says whether a format may read copy_file directly, so the contract for the I/O layer is undefined.

refuted.title: Only a NOTICE-only in-tree module checks the custom format API
refuted.failure_scenario: A committer pushes v3 with test_copy_custom_format as its only in-tree user. A later refactor of copyto.c or copyfromparse.c breaks the byte I/O path for custom formats. No test fails, and authors of Arrow or JSON lines extensions find the break after the release ships.
refuted.argument: In [P8], a small custom-scan example was rejected because it did not show that real use cases keep working. The same applies here. The test module only raises NOTICEs, and message #340 shows why that hid a real gap: v3 does not export CopySendData() or CopyGetData(), so no extension can move bytes. Messages #340 and #341 found this with out-of-tree code, and the in-tree module still fails on master.
refuted.author_must_show: Will the patch set add an in-tree format that writes and reads real rows through every COPY source and destination, so that a broken export or callback fails a test?

precedents.title: ctidscan as an example of custom-scan

critic.reasoning: Duplicate of maintenance-fit-3, which makes the same point and also cites [P3], where reviewers asked for an in-tree user of a COPY callback.

refuted.title: Core text/CSV options are silently accepted with a custom format
refuted.failure_scenario: A user runs COPY t TO 'f' WITH (FORMAT ndjson, HEADER true, DELIMITER '|') and gets no error, and the options have no effect. The user finds out only by reading the output file. If a later release starts rejecting these options, scripts that ran without error start to fail after upgrade.
refuted.argument: Message #341 shows that DELIMITER, HEADER, NULL and FORCE_QUOTE are accepted with FORMAT ndjson and change nothing. The reason is that the text/CSV checks are skipped when CopyFormatIsBuiltin() is false. Today COPY rejects an option that does not apply to the chosen format, for example HEADER with binary. v3 makes each extension responsible for keeping that rule, and an extension that does nothing breaks the rule. Once released, ignoring these options becomes behaviour that users depend on.
refuted.author_must_show: Which core options does core reject for a custom format, and how does a format declare the core options it accepts?

critic.reasoning: Duplicate of maintenance-fit-2, which covers the same silently accepted text/CSV options and adds ON_ERROR and future options.

refuted.title: Format names share one global namespace with future core formats
refuted.failure_scenario: An extension registers FORMAT 'json', and a later release adds a built-in json format. After upgrade, scripts that ran COPY ... (FORMAT json) either silently get the core output, which may differ from the extension's, or the extension fails to load because its name is now reserved. The DBA finds out from a changed output file or a failed LOAD.
refuted.argument: Message #282 raised this collision. JSON output from COPY in core is one of the cited demands in message #1. Message #284 left the risk to extension authors, and message #294 chose _PG_init() registration without stating a naming rule. A committer would likely ask for a rule now, such as a reserved prefix, a documented list of names core may take, or an error on collision, because changing name resolution after release breaks existing scripts.
refuted.author_must_show: What rule stops a registered format name from colliding with a format that core adds later, and what happens to existing COPY commands when it does?

critic.reasoning: Messages #279, #284, #286 and #294 weighed this collision and chose a flat name space where built-in names win and duplicates raise an error. Custom EXPLAIN options and logical decoding plugins follow the same rule, and the cost falls on users of the extension.

refuted.title: Objects that name a custom format do not restore unless the library is preloaded
refuted.failure_scenario: A DBA creates a file_fdw foreign table with OPTIONS (format 'ndjson'). pg_dump emits that option, and pg_restore into a cluster where the library is not in shared_preload_libraries or session_preload_libraries fails with 'COPY format "ndjson" not recognized'. The DBA finds out during restore or pg_upgrade.
refuted.argument: Message #341 confirms that file_fdw accepts a custom format and that FORMAT fails in a session that has not loaded the library. Registration happens only in _PG_init(), with no catalog entry and no dependency. So CREATE EXTENSION does not make the format available, pg_dump cannot order or record it, and no view lists the registered formats. The format ID view was deferred in message #296.
refuted.author_must_show: How does a dump that references a custom format, for example in file_fdw options, restore reliably, and how can a user see which formats are registered?

critic.reasoning: Duplicate of replication-ondisk-1. Its claim that CREATE EXTENSION never makes the format available is also too strong, because creating a C function loads the library in that session.

refuted.title: Exposing the full COPY state structs freezes their layout as ABI
refuted.failure_scenario: A minor-release bug fix adds a field in the middle of CopyFromStateData. An Arrow extension built against the earlier minor release reads format_private or copy_file at a shifted offset and crashes or corrupts its output. Nothing fails at build time, so users find out in production after the upgrade.
refuted.argument: Message #336 drops the earlier split and moves the whole of CopyFromStateData and CopyToStateData into copy_state.h, including buffers that only the built-in parsers use. Message #314 lists broken ABI on field changes as a known cost of this approach. Message #309 asks which COPY improvements this forecloses, and every future change to these structs now has to respect extension layout. Other exposed structs live with the same rule, but the proposal does not state which fields are a supported contract.
refuted.author_must_show: Which fields of the exported COPY state structs are a stable contract for extensions, and how will backpatched fixes avoid changing their offsets?

critic.reasoning: Messages #321, #327 and #336 weighed full exposure and chose it to match existing practice such as table AM scan descriptors. The rule against adding fields mid-struct in a minor release already applies to every installed header, as the objection itself notes.

refuted.title: Core does not keep custom formats inside the COPY column list
refuted.failure_scenario: A role has INSERT only on t(a) and runs copy t(a) from ... with (format ndjson). The format maps JSON keys to relation columns by name, so it also fills column b, which has no default. The row is stored with a value in b that the role may not write, and nothing in core reports it.
refuted.argument: Column privileges are checked against the COPY column list, but CopyFromOneRow receives the full values/nulls arrays and the relation. On COPY TO from a table, the slot passed to the format holds every column, so emitting all slot attributes would leak columns the user cannot SELECT. Manu's module honours the column list (message #340), but only by its own choice. Message #341 already asks for written callback contracts, and this one bears on privileges, not only on correctness.
refuted.author_must_show: Will core reset or ignore values for columns outside attnumlist after CopyFromOneRow, and hand COPY TO formats only listed columns, or how else is the column-privilege invariant kept?

critic.reasoning: The scenario needs a format that ignores attnumlist, and the only module in the material honours it (message #340). Postgres trusts loaded C code in the same way for FDWs and table AMs, so this is an extension bug that core does not guard against elsewhere.

refuted.title: Whole COPY state structs become extension ABI with no boundary
refuted.failure_scenario: A later release reorders or renames a field in CopyFromStateData, for example in the raw_buf or line_buf group, to speed up text parsing. A Parquet or Arrow extension built against the old copy_state.h still compiles or loads, then reads the wrong field. Users see wrong rows or a crash after a minor or major upgrade.
refuted.argument: Message #336 drops the earlier split that hid internal fields, and 0001 moves both full structs into a public header. Every field becomes something extensions may touch, and no list says which fields are supported. Messages #314 and #315 had worked out a minimal public set (rel, attnumlist, opts, error-context fields), but v3 does not use it.
refuted.author_must_show: Which CopyFromStateData and CopyToStateData fields are a supported interface for formats, and how will a change to the other fields be signalled to extension authors?

critic.reasoning: The scenario cannot happen as written. A renamed field fails at compile time, the module magic check stops a library built for another major version from loading, and minor releases do not reorder struct fields. Message #336 dropped the split on purpose.

touch_points.label: on-disk format / pg_upgrade
touch_points.reason: file_fdw stores a custom format name in its options, and pg_upgrade's schema restore must resolve it.

touch_points.label: wire protocol
touch_points.reason: COPY TO STDOUT and FROM STDIN with a custom format send CopyOutResponse and CopyInResponse format codes.

touch_points.label: catalog changes
touch_points.reason: see objection replication-ondisk-1: Custom format names stored in file_fdw options have no catalog anchor

touch_points.label: ABI / extension API
touch_points.reason: RegisterCopyCustomFormat(), copy_state.h with both COPY state structs, and proposed exports of the COPY I/O functions.

touch_points.label: SQL-standard conflict or non-standard syntax
touch_points.reason: The COPY option FORMAT accepts names registered by a loaded extension.

touch_points.label: pg_dump / restore round-trip
touch_points.reason: pg_dump emits file_fdw options that name a custom format, which restores only when the library is loaded.

touch_points.label: psql UX conventions
touch_points.reason: \copy passes a custom format through the frontend path; message #341 tested it only with a text format.

touch_points.label: security / privileges
touch_points.reason: Format code loaded through _PG_init() receives the relation and the full values arrays during COPY.

touch_points.label: backpatchability
touch_points.reason: Fields of the exported COPY state structs constrain what minor-release fixes may change.

touch_points.label: maintenance burden ("who maintains this in 10 years")
touch_points.reason: Every future COPY option and every change to COPY buffering must consider out-of-tree formats.

touch_points.label: performance on the hot path
touch_points.reason: Built-in text, csv and binary COPY run through the callback routines; benchmarks showed differences mostly within 5%.

touch_points.label: doesn't fit what Postgres is about (extension / external tool / already solved)

questions: What rule makes core reject a COPY option, including ON_ERROR, DELIMITER and future options, that a custom format does not declare support for?
Will the series include an in-tree format that reads and writes real rows through the exported I/O functions on file, frontend and PROGRAM paths?
How does a file_fdw table that names a custom format survive pg_dump, pg_restore and pg_upgrade when the library is not preloaded?
Which overall and per-column format codes does the server send in CopyOutResponse and CopyInResponse for a custom format, and who chooses them?
May a COPY FROM format read copy_file directly, and which changes to COPY buffering stay possible once CopyGetData and CopySendData are exported?

committability.owner_note: Sawada writes the current v3 series and Paquier supported the _PG_init() design. The owner needs to know the COPY code and extension API practice.
committability.liability: The owner signs for a permanent extension API: the registration function, the exposed COPY state structs, the exported I/O functions and the option rules. Later COPY changes must keep out-of-tree formats working.
committability.author_follow_up: The author has moved the entry through 13 CommitFests since 2023 and replies in the thread. v3 needs a rebase, and the reviews in messages #340 and #341 have no visible answer yet.

priority.reason: Demand for JSON lines, Arrow and Parquet has lasted since 2018 and a committer writes the series. The open points are the option rule, a real in-tree format, the I/O contract and the protocol format code, across a 341-message thread.

provisional_note: The code was not read, and only 3 of 341 messages were visible directly. The per-row cost for built-in formats, the exact option checks in v3 and the format codes sent to the client could not be checked.
disclosure: Prepared by an AI harness; treat as a devil's advocate, not a verdict.

precedents_retrieved.title: Allow COPY "text" to output a header and add header matching mode to COPY FROM
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch lets COPY write and read a HEADER line in the text format, which before was allowed only in CSV mode. A later version also adds HEADER match to COPY FROM, which requires the header line to match the target column names in both text and CSV format.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Michael Paquier returned the patch with feedback after the v5 revision. He judged it wrong to treat HEADER as a boolean-like option with one extra "match" value, and suggested a separate option for clear semantics. He also asked that repeated HEADER options be detected as redundant, as COPY does for "format". The first 2018 version was returned earlier because his review, which also raised header matching, was not addressed.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
It seems to me that we may
actually be looking at having this stuff as an option different than
"header" at the end to have clear semantics.

precedents_retrieved.title: Allow COPY's 'text' format to output a header
precedents_retrieved.summary: Allow the HEADER option of COPY with the default text format, so COPY TO writes a line of column names and COPY FROM skips it. Before the patch, HEADER worked only in CSV format.
precedents_retrieved.objection: After the patch reached Ready for Committer, Michael Paquier posted a new review. It asked for different error wording, a round-trip export and import test for text and CSV, an update to header_line in CopyStateData (which still assumed CSV only), and file_fdw tests. The author did not answer for several weeks, so Michael Paquier marked the patch returned with feedback.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
It has been a couple of weeks since the last review, which has not been
addressed, so I am marking the patch as returned with feedback.

precedents_retrieved.title: Adding Support for Copy callback functionality on COPY TO api
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch adds a data destination callback to the COPY TO API, matching the data source callback that COPY FROM already has. Extensions could then use COPY TO to send rows to their own destinations, for example for storage, backup or analytics.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The author did not answer review feedback for two weeks, so the patch was returned with feedback. The open review points were to run pgindent, to add an in-tree user of the callback, and to have the callback return the number of bytes written and report failure.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
This feedback has not been answered after two weeks, so I have marked
the patch as returned with feedback.

precedents_retrieved.title: Custom signals and handlers for extension
precedents_retrieved.authors: Maksim Milyutin (maksm90), Alexey Kondratov (ololobus), Pavel Borisov (pborisov)
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch lets shared-preload extensions reserve custom ProcSignal slots from a fixed set and register handler functions for them. A backend can then send such a signal to another backend, where the handler runs at CHECK_FOR_INTERRUPTS, giving extensions like pg_query_state a low-level RPC mechanism without patching core.
precedents_retrieved.objection: In 2018 the author did not respond to review for weeks, then said he wanted to rework the design and could not finish for that release, so it was returned with feedback. In 2020 Michael Paquier objected to a revived version because it had no test module and no documentation. He also objected to the hardcoded limit of 64 custom signals and asked for a flexible registration of custom procsignals at shmem init time.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
Second, it uses
a hardcoded custom number of signals of 64 instead of a flexible
design.

precedents_retrieved.title: csv output format for psql
precedents_retrieved.summary: Add a CSV output format to psql (\pset format csv, plus a --csv command-line option) that applies CSV quoting rules to query and meta-command output, as an alternative to COPY/\copy for producing CSV. Later versions introduced a separate fieldsep_csv variable defaulting to a comma, with validation of allowed separator values.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The entry was returned with feedback because, after the last review in late August 2018, the patch was waiting for a response from the author and no new version was posted. Earlier disagreements over field-separator handling appear to have been settled by the fieldsep_csv design, which Pavel Stehule accepted; the last review asked for an added test for rejected fieldsep_csv values.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
The patch has been waiting for input from the author since August, so I
am marking it as returned with feedback.

precedents_retrieved.title: copy_srf (was COPY as a set returning function)
precedents_retrieved.summary: Add a core set-returning function copy_srf() that reads a file or program output with the COPY FROM machinery and returns the rows to a query, so users can select or filter them without a temp table or a file_fdw table. Later versions added a TupleDesc parameter to BeginCopy() and BeginCopyFrom() so COPY can run without a relation in pg_class.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Michael Paquier closed it as immature because the new rsTupDesc parameter overlaps with the relation that callers already pass to BeginCopyFrom(), and because the function used NextCopyFromRawFields and skipped the checks in NextCopyFrom(). The author had not chosen between a function, a RETURNING clause on COPY, or an extension hook, and reviewers asked for tests and documentation. Copy from STDIN also failed with a protocol error.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
Looking at the last patch proposed, I find the current patch proposed
as immature, as rsTupDesc basically overlaps with the relation a
caller can define in BeginCopyFrom(), so marking this patch as
"returned with feedback".

precedents_retrieved.title: Fix formatting of Interval output
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch special-cased INT_MIN hours in EncodeInterval, so that abs() no longer prints a value such as '--2147483648:00:00'. It fixed only that one output path.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Tom Lane noted that three of the four formats in EncodeInterval assume -x or abs(x) is safe, and that interval2tm can overflow on values Postgres computed successfully, so fixing one symptom was not enough. He suggested int64 arithmetic in a new struct for intervals in place of struct pg_tm. The author withdrew the entry and moved the work to his related commitfest patch 3541.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: Not much point in fixing only one symptom.

precedents_retrieved.title: ctidscan as an example of custom-scan
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch adds ctidscan, an example custom-scan provider that scans only part of a table when the query has inequality conditions on the ctid system column, with an enable_ctidscan setting. Its main purpose is to serve as sample code and a test for the custom-scan interface, possibly placed in src/test/modules.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Tom Lane argued that the custom-scan interface cannot support anything of real interest, so a small example like ctidscan does not show that real use cases keep working. He added that the ctid range use case would need less new code as an extension of TidScan. The visible messages end in a broader debate about custom-scan APIs and do not show a separate decision on this patch.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
So a finger
exercise like ctidscan, even though it might have some marginal use,
doesn't do much to alleviate that concern.  It certainly doesn't seem
like it's a suitable placeholder proving that we aren't breaking any
actual use cases for the feature.

Revert "Change SHA2 implementation based on OpenSSL to use EVP digest routines"
Reverted commit(s): Change SHA2 implementation based on OpenSSL to use EVP digest routines
precedents_retrieved.objection:
This reverts commit e21cbb4, as the switch to EVP routines requires a
more careful design where we would need to have at least our wrapper
routines return a status instead of issuing an error by themselves to
let the caller do the error handling.  The memory handling was also
incorrect and could cause leaks in the backend if a failure happened,
requiring most likely a callback to do the necessary cleanup as the only
clean way to be able to allocate an EVP context requires the use of an
allocation within OpenSSL.  The potential rework of the wrappers also
impacts the fallback implementation when not building with OpenSSL.

Originally, prairiedog has reported a compilation failure, but after
discussion with Tom Lane this needs a better design.

roaster_notes.note: No listed precedent rejected extensible COPY formats as an idea. The COPY RAW rows [P11], [P14] and [P16] add a built-in format and record no reason, so they were not used. Message #1 cites earlier threads that it says reached consensus on extensibility, conditional on showing no performance loss.
The proposal adds no WAL records, on-disk relation format or catalog. Logical replication table sync and pg_dump data use unqualified text, which always resolves to the built-in format.
Loading through _PG_init() keeps format code under administrator control. Built-in names cannot be shadowed, and core still checks file and program privileges, so I see no other exposure.
Owner signal is good: Sawada, a committer, writes the current series, and Paquier supported the _PG_init design. The per-row cost claim is plausible because v3 changes only option processing.

Existing tools do not cover the main use case. An FDW such as parquet_fdw (message #10) or COPY (SELECT row_to_json(...)) can handle server-side files or JSON output, but neither can stream Arrow or Parquet through COPY FROM STDIN or TO STDOUT over the frontend protocol. Committers have supported moving formats into extensions since 2018 (messages #1, #294), so this angle finds no objection.

The material shows lasting, independent demand: requests for JSON lines, Arrow, Avro, Parquet and ORC from 2018, 2022 and 2023 (message #1), with working extensions for Arrow and JSON lines and a user-side Parquet request (message #341). Committers are engaged, and an existing FDW workaround (message #10) does not cover COPY's role in loading and unloading data.
